label: def:corridor
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:corridor}
Fix the middle-straight parameter $M>0$ and set $y_t:=1+M$.  Define the
closed sets
\begin{align*}
S_X &:= (-\infty,0]\times[0,1]\times[0,1] && \text{(entry arm)},\\
S_Y &:= [0,1]\times[0,\,y_t]\times[0,1] && \text{(middle arm)},\\
S_Z &:= [0,1]\times[y_t,\,y_t+1]\times[0,\infty) && \text{(exit arm)},
\end{align*}
and the \emph{corridor} $K=K_M:=S_X\cupS_Y\cupS_Z$, a closed connected set.
The cube $[0,1]^3$ (the $y\le1$ end of $S_Y$) is the \emph{first corner cube},
where the turn from the $-x$ direction to the $+y$ direction happens (a turn
in the $x$--$y$ plane); the cube $[0,1]\times[y_t,y_t+1]\times[0,1]$ (the
$z\le1$ end of $S_Z$) is the \emph{second corner cube}, where the turn from
$+y$ to $+z$ happens (a turn in the $y$--$z$ plane); between them lies the
clear middle straight $[0,1]\times[1,y_t]\times[0,1]$ of length $M$.  The
value in the code accompanying Problem~6.64 of \cite{GGTW25} is $M=4$.
For $c\in[0,y_t]$ write $\mathrm{Stub}(c):=[0,1]\times[0,c]\times[0,1]\subseteqS_Y$.
head: environment

label: def:traversal
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:traversal}
A \emph{body} is a compact connected set $B\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ with $\operatorname{vol}(B)>0$.  A
\emph{motion} is a continuous map $g:[0,1]\to SE(3)$ (matrix topology),
written $g_t(p)=R_tp+v_t$ with $R_t\in SO(3)$; put $B_t:=g_t(B)$.  The pair
$(B,g)$ \emph{traverses $K_M$ weakly} if
\[
\text{(i) } B_t\subseteqK_M\ \ \forall t\in[0,1];\qquad
\text{(ii) } B_0\subseteqS_X;\qquad
\text{(iii) } B_1\subseteqS_Z ,
\]
and \emph{strongly} if moreover $B_1\subseteqS_Z\cap\{z\ge1\}$ (entirely past
the second corner cube, from where a pure $+z$ translation exits to
infinity).  The objective is
\[
V^{*}(K_M):=\sup\{\operatorname{vol}(B):\ (B,g)\text{ traverses } K_M \text{ weakly}\}.
\]
head: environment
name: traversal; the objective

label: rem:wlog
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:wlog}
(a) Strong traversal implies weak, so every upper bound proved for weak
traversal covers both readings, as well as the instantiation in the code of
\cite{GGTW25}, whose fixed start and end poses satisfy (ii) and the strong
form of (iii).
(b) Requiring $B$ compact loses no generality: if $B$ is merely bounded,
connected and measurable, its closure $\overline{B}$ is compact and connected,
$\operatorname{vol}(\overline B)\ge\operatorname{vol}(B)$, and
$g_t(\overline B)=\overline{g_t(B)}\subseteq\overline{K}=K$ (the corridor
and the arms $S_X,S_Z$ are closed), so $(\overline B,g)$ traverses whenever
$(B,g)$ does.  Hence the supremum over bounded connected sets equals the
supremum over bodies.
(c) No existence of a maximizer is assumed anywhere below; all bounds cap the
supremum directly.
(d) The experiments of \cite{GGTW25} restrict to bodies inside a
$4\times1\times1$ block and to one fixed pair of endpoint poses.  These are
restrictions of the search class, legitimate for lower bounds; none of them
may be (or is) used in the upper-bound proofs below.
head: environment
name: weak traversal suffices; compactness is no loss

label: def:tubedef
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:tubedef}
A \emph{tube} is a rigid image of $\mathbb{R}\times[0,1]^2$: a set
\[
T=\{\rho+s\,w+\alpha f_1+\beta f_2:\ s\in\mathbb{R},\ |\alpha|\le\tfrac12,\
|\beta|\le\tfrac12\},
\]
where $w$ (the \emph{axis direction}) and $f_1,f_2$ form an orthonormal
frame and $\rho\in\mathbb{R}^3$.  Its cross-section is a unit square of diameter
$\sqrt2$; a tube is closed and convex.  Points of $T$ decompose uniquely as
$\rho+s w+\xi$ with $\xi\perp w$, $\xi$ in the cross-section square
$Q:=\{\alpha f_1+\beta f_2:|\alpha|,|\beta|\le\frac12\}$, and
$|\xi|\le\sqrt2/2$.
head: environment
name: tube

label: lem:tube
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:tube}
For every $t\in[0,1]$,
\[
B_t\;\subseteq\;T(t):=g_t\,g_0^{-1}\bigl(\mathbb{R}\times[0,1]^2\bigr),
\]
a tube with axis direction $w(t):=R_tR_0^{-1}\hat{x}$.  Moreover
$B_t\subseteq g_tg_0^{-1}(S_X)$ (a half-tube) and, symmetrically,
$B_t\subseteq g_tg_1^{-1}(S_Z)$, so $B_t$ also lies in a tube with axis
$R_tR_1^{-1}\hat{z}$.
head: environment
name: tube confinement

title: Proof
body_md:
$B_0=g_0(B)\subseteqS_X\subseteq\mathbb{R}\times[0,1]^2$, hence
$B\subseteq g_0^{-1}(\mathbb{R}\times[0,1]^2)$ and
$B_t=g_t(B)\subseteq g_tg_0^{-1}(\mathbb{R}\times[0,1]^2)$, which is a rigid image of
the standard tube with axis $\hat{x}$, hence a tube with axis direction
$R_tR_0^{-1}\hat{x}$.  The refinements use
$B_0\subseteq S_X$ and $B_1\subseteq S_Z\subseteq[0,1]\times[y_t,y_t+1]\times\mathbb{R}$
verbatim.
head: environment

label: lem:cont
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: continuity of the height profile

title: Proof
body_md:
$B$ is compact, so the maxima exist.  For $s,t\in[0,1]$ and any $p\in B$,
$|g_t(p)-g_s(p)|\le\|R_t-R_s\|_{\mathrm{op}}\max_{q\in B}|q|+|v_t-v_s|=:
\omega(s,t)$, so $\mathcal M(t)\le\mathcal M(s)+\omega(s,t)$ and symmetrically;
$g$ is continuous on the compact interval $[0,1]$, hence uniformly continuous,
so $\omega(s,t)\to0$ as $|s-t|\to0$.  The same bound handles $m$.
head: environment

label: lem:event
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:event}
Let $c\in(1,y_t)$.  There is a first time $\tau_c\in(0,1)$ with
$\mathcal M(\tau_c)=c$, and at it
\[
B_{\tau_c}\subseteq K\cap\{y\le c\}=S_X\cup\mathrm{Stub}(c),
\]
and there exists a touch point $q\in B_{\tau_c}$ with
\[
q\cdot\hat{y}=c,\qquad q\in[0,1]\times\{c\}\times[0,1].
\]
head: environment
name: first-crossing event

title: Proof
body_md:
$\mathcal M(0)\le1<c$ since $B_0\subseteqS_X\subseteq\{y\le1\}$, and
$\mathcal M(1)\ge y_t>c$ since $B_1\subseteqS_Z\subseteq\{y\ge y_t\}$ and $B$
is nonempty.  The set $\{t:\mathcal M(t)\ge c\}$ is closed (Lemma
\ref{lem:cont}), nonempty ($t=1$), and does not contain $0$; let $\tau_c$ be
its minimum.  Then $\mathcal M(\tau_c)\ge c$; if $\mathcal M(\tau_c)>c$, the
intermediate value theorem on $[0,\tau_c]$ would produce an earlier time in
the set, contradicting minimality; hence $\mathcal M(\tau_c)=c$.  Thus every
point of $B_{\tau_c}$ has $y\le c$, and $B_{\tau_c}\subseteqK$, so
\eqref{eq:Kfacts} gives the containment.  By compactness the maximum is
attained at some $q\in B_{\tau_c}$ with $q\cdot\hat{y}=c>1$; since
$S_X\subseteq\{y\le1\}$, necessarily $q\in\mathrm{Stub}(c)$, i.e.\
$q_x,q_z\in[0,1]$.
head: environment

label: lem:deep
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:deep}
Let $c\in(1,y_t)$ and $\tau_c$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:event}, and suppose in
addition that $B_{\tau_c}\cap\{y\le1\}\neq\emptyset$.  Then there exists
$p^*\in B_{\tau_c}$ with
\[
p^*\cdot\hat{y}=1,\qquad p^*\in[0,1]\times\{1\}\times[0,1].
\]
head: environment
name: deep point

title: Proof
body_md:
$B_{\tau_c}$ is compact and connected, so its image under $p\mapsto
p\cdot\hat{y}$ is a compact interval; it contains a value $\le1$ (hypothesis)
and the value $c>1$ (touch point), hence contains $[1,c]$.  For each
$\delta\in(0,c-1]$ pick $p_\delta\in B_{\tau_c}$ with $p_\delta\cdot\hat{y}
=1+\delta$.  By Lemma~\ref{lem:event}, $p_\delta\inS_X\cup\mathrm{Stub}(c)$, and
$y(p_\delta)>1$ rules out $S_X$; so $p_\delta\in\mathrm{Stub}(c)$, i.e.\
$(p_\delta)_x,(p_\delta)_z\in[0,1]$.  Let $\delta\downarrow0$ along a
sequence for which $p_\delta$ converges (compactness); the limit $p^*$ lies
in the closed set $B_{\tau_c}$, has $p^*\cdot\hat{y}=1$, and has
$p^*_x,p^*_z\in[0,1]$ (closed conditions).
head: environment

label: lem:tilt
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:tilt}
Let $c=1+u$ with $u\in(\sqrt2,\,M)$, let $\tau_c,q$ be as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:event}, and assume the deep-point hypothesis
$B_{\tau_c}\cap\{y\le1\}\neq\emptyset$.  Then
\[
\mu\;\ge\;\mu_{\mathrm{lin}}(u):=\frac{u-\sqrt2}{\sqrt{2+u^2}}\;>\;0 .
\]
head: environment
name: tilt

label: eq:qpstar
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $p^*$ be the deep point of Lemma~\ref{lem:deep} and write $w:=w(\tau_c)$.
Both $q,p^*\in T(\tau_c)$; decompose (Definition~\ref{def:tubedef})
\[
q-p^*=\sigma w+\eta,\qquad \eta\perp w,
\]
where $\sigma\in\mathbb{R}$ is the difference of axis parameters and $\eta$ the
difference of two cross-section vectors, so $|\eta|\le\sqrt2$ (diameter of the
unit square).  The coordinate differences satisfy $|\Delta x|\le1$,
$\Delta y=c-1=u$, $|\Delta z|\le1$, hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qpstar}
\sigma^2+|\eta|^2=|q-p^*|^2\le 2+u^2 .
\end{equation}
Now project onto $\hat{y}$:
\[
u=(q-p^*)\cdot\hat{y}=\sigma\,(w\cdot\hat{y})+\eta\cdot\hat{y}
\le|\sigma|\,\mu+|\eta|
\le\sqrt{2+u^2}\,\mu+\sqrt2 ,
\]
and rearranging gives the claim (positivity because $u>\sqrt2$).
head: environment

label: lem:slab
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:slab}
Let $T$ be a tube with axis direction $w$ and $\mu:=|w\cdot\hat{y}|>0$.  Then
\[
\operatorname{vol}\bigl(T\cap\{0\le y\le1\}\bigr)\;\le\;\frac{1+\sqrt2}{\mu}.
\]
head: environment
name: tube--slab estimate

title: Proof
body_md:
Write points of $T$ as $p=\rho+s\,w+\xi$ with $\xi\in Q$, $|\xi|\le\sqrt2/2$
(Definition~\ref{def:tubedef}).  Then
$p\cdot\hat{y}=\rho\cdot\hat{y}+s\,(w\cdot\hat{y})+\xi\cdot\hat{y}$ with
$|\xi\cdot\hat{y}|\le\sqrt2/2$, so $p\cdot\hat{y}\in[0,1]$ forces
$s\,(w\cdot\hat{y})$ into an interval of length $1+\sqrt2$, i.e.\ $s$ into an
interval $I$ with $|I|\le(1+\sqrt2)/\mu$.  Hence
$T\cap\{0\le y\le1\}\subseteq\{\rho+sw+\xi:\ s\in I,\ \xi\in Q\}$, whose
volume is $|I|\cdot\operatorname{area}(Q)=|I|\le(1+\sqrt2)/\mu$ (the map
$(s,\xi)\mapsto\rho+sw+\xi$ is an isometry of $\mathbb{R}\times Q$ onto its image).
head: environment

label: thm:A
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:A}
Let $M>\sqrt2$ and let $(B,g)$ traverse $K_M$ weakly.  Then for every
$u\in(\sqrt2,M)$,
\[
\operatorname{vol}(B)\;\le\;f(u):=u+(1+\sqrt2)\,\frac{\sqrt{2+u^2}}{u-\sqrt2}.
\]
In particular, taking $u=3.5217$,
\[
V^{*}(K_M)\;\le\;f(3.5217)=7.86908\ldots\;<\;7.8691
\qquad\text{for every } M\ge3.53 ,
\]
covering the corridor of Problem~6.64 ($M=4$) and every larger $M$.
head: environment
name: first upper bound

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $u\in(\sqrt2,M)$ and set $c:=1+u\in(1+\sqrt2,\,y_t)$.  Apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:event} at height $c$ and write $B':=B_{\tau_c}$, so
$\operatorname{vol}(B')=\operatorname{vol}(B)$ and $B'\subseteqS_X\cup\mathrm{Stub}(c)$.

\emph{Case (i): $B'\cap\{y\le1\}=\emptyset$.}  Every point of $B'$ has $y>1$,
which rules out all of $S_X$; hence $B'\subseteq\mathrm{Stub}(c)\cap\{y>1\}
=[0,1]\times(1,c]\times[0,1]$ and $\operatorname{vol}(B)\le u\le f(u)$.

\emph{Case (ii): $B'\cap\{y\le1\}\neq\emptyset$.}  By Lemma~\ref{lem:tilt}
the tube $T:=T(\tau_c)\supseteq B'$ has $\mu\ge\mu_{\mathrm{lin}}(u)>0$.
Split $B'$ along the plane $\{y=1\}$:
\[
\operatorname{vol}(B'\cap\{y\le1\})\le
\operatorname{vol}\bigl(T\cap\{0\le y\le1\}\bigr)\le\frac{1+\sqrt2}{\mu}
\le\frac{1+\sqrt2}{\mu_{\mathrm{lin}}(u)},
\]
using $B'\subseteqK\subseteq\{y\ge0\}$ \eqref{eq:Kfacts} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:slab}, and
\[
\operatorname{vol}(B'\cap\{y>1\})\le\operatorname{vol}\bigl(\mathrm{Stub}(c)\cap\{y>1\}\bigr)=u ,
\]
since $S_X\cap\{y>1\}=\emptyset$.  Adding,
$\operatorname{vol}(B)\le u+(1+\sqrt2)/\mu_{\mathrm{lin}}(u)=f(u)$.

For the numerical form: if $M\ge3.53$ then $u=3.5217<3.53\le M$ is
admissible, and a direct evaluation gives $f(3.5217)=7.8690829\ldots<7.8691$.
head: environment

label: rem:optA
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:optA}
The function $f$ decreases from $+\infty$ (as $u\downarrow\sqrt2$) to its
minimum $7.869083\ldots$, attained near $u=3.5215$, and then increases;
any admissible $u$ near the minimizer gives the same bound to the quoted
precision.  For $M\in(\sqrt2,3.53)$ the theorem still applies with any
$u<M$ and yields $V^{*}(K_M)\le\inf_{u\in(\sqrt2,M)}f(u)=f(M)$ (the
infimum is a limit of admissible values; $f$ is decreasing there); the bound
blows up as $M\downarrow\sqrt2$, since the mechanism needs stub room above
height $1+\sqrt2$.
head: environment
name: optimization; smaller $M$

label: lem:tiltsharp
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:tiltsharp}
Under the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:tilt},
\[
\mu\;\ge\;\mu_*(u):=\frac{u^2-2}{u^2+2}\;>\;0 .
\]
head: environment
name: sharp tilt

label: eq:umax
title: Proof
body_md:
Keep the notation of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:tilt}, write
$A:=\sqrt{2+u^2}$, and set $s:=|\sigma|\ge0$, $h:=|\eta|\in[0,\sqrt2]$.
Since $\eta\perp w$, we have $\eta\cdot\hat{y}=\eta\cdot P\hat{y}$, where $P$ is
the orthogonal projection onto $w^\perp$ and $|P\hat{y}|=\sqrt{1-\mu^2}$; hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:umax}
u\;\le\;s\,\mu+h\sqrt{1-\mu^2},\qquad s^2+h^2\le A^2,\qquad 0\le h\le\sqrt2 .
\end{equation}
First, an algebraic preliminary: $\mu_*(u)\le u/A$, because squaring the
equivalent inequality $(u^2-2)A\le u(u^2+2)$ reduces it to
$(u^2-2)^2\le u^2(u^2+2)$, i.e.\ $4\le6u^2$, true for $u>\sqrt2$.

Suppose now, for contradiction, that $\mu<\mu_*(u)$; then also $\mu<u/A$.
Bound the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:umax} over all admissible $(s,h)$: for
fixed $h$, the largest admissible $s$ is $\sqrt{A^2-h^2}$, giving
$\varphi(h):=\mu\sqrt{A^2-h^2}+h\sqrt{1-\mu^2}$, and
\[
\varphi'(h)=\sqrt{1-\mu^2}-\frac{\mu h}{\sqrt{A^2-h^2}}\ \ge\ 0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad h^2\le A^2(1-\mu^2),
\]
which holds for all $h\in[0,\sqrt2]$ because $\mu<u/A$ gives
$A^2(1-\mu^2)>A^2-u^2=2\ge h^2$.  So $\varphi$ is nondecreasing on
$[0,\sqrt2]$ and
\[
s\,\mu+h\sqrt{1-\mu^2}\;\le\;\varphi(\sqrt2)=u\,\mu+\sqrt2\sqrt{1-\mu^2}
\]
(using $\sqrt{A^2-2}=u$).  Finally let
$\psi(\mu):=u\mu+\sqrt2\sqrt{1-\mu^2}-u$.  Then $\psi(\mu_*(u))=0$: indeed
$1-\mu_*^2=8u^2/(u^2+2)^2$, so
$\sqrt2\sqrt{1-\mu_*^2}=4u/(u^2+2)=u(1-\mu_*)$.  Moreover
$\psi'(\mu)=u-\sqrt2\,\mu/\sqrt{1-\mu^2}>0$ iff $\mu<u/A$, so $\psi$ is
strictly increasing on $[0,u/A]$, and $\mu<\mu_*(u)\le u/A$ gives
$\psi(\mu)<0$, i.e.\ $u\mu+\sqrt2\sqrt{1-\mu^2}<u$.  Combining the two
displays contradicts \eqref{eq:umax}.  Hence $\mu\ge\mu_*(u)$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
$\mu_*(u)\ge\mu_{\mathrm{lin}}(u)$ for all $u\ge\sqrt2$: dividing the claim
$\frac{(u-\sqrt2)(u+\sqrt2)}{u^2+2}\ge\frac{u-\sqrt2}{\sqrt{u^2+2}}$ by
$u-\sqrt2\ge0$ leaves $(u+\sqrt2)\ge\sqrt{u^2+2}$, i.e.\ $2\sqrt2u\ge0$.  So
Lemma~\ref{lem:tiltsharp} strictly sharpens Lemma~\ref{lem:tilt} for
$u>\sqrt2$ (e.g.\ at $u=3.52$: $0.722$ versus $0.555$), and
Theorem~\ref{thm:A} could already be improved by substituting it; we do not
record the intermediate constant, since the chord estimates below give more.
head: environment

label: lem:chord
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:chord}
Let $T$ be a tube with axis direction $w$ (Definition~\ref{def:tubedef}) and
let $v$ be a unit vector with $v\neq\pm w$.  Then every line parallel to $v$
meets $T$ in a segment of length at most
$\sqrt2/|Pv|$, where $P$ is the orthogonal projection onto $w^{\perp}$ and
$|Pv|=\sqrt{1-(w\cdot v)^2}$.
Consequently, for any choice of two coordinate directions
$e_i,e_j\in\{\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z}\}$, $i\ne j$, with remaining direction $e_k$
and $w\neq\pm e_k$:
\[
\operatorname{vol}\Bigl(T\cap\{p:\ (p\cdot e_i,\ p\cdot e_j)\in[0,1]^2\}\Bigr)
\;\le\;\frac{\sqrt2}{\sqrt{1-(w\cdot e_k)^2}}
=\frac{\sqrt2}{\sqrt{(w\cdot e_i)^2+(w\cdot e_j)^2}} .
\]
head: environment
name: chord estimate for tubes

title: Proof
body_md:
$T$ is convex, so a line $\ell:t\mapsto p_0+t\,v$ meets it in a (possibly
empty or degenerate) segment.  Membership of $p$ in $T$ depends only on
$P(p-\rho)$, which must lie in the cross-section square $Q$
(Definition~\ref{def:tubedef}); along $\ell$, $P(p_0+tv-\rho)$ moves on a
line in the cross-plane with speed $|Pv|>0$, and its time inside the square
is at most $\operatorname{diam}(Q)/|Pv|=\sqrt2/|Pv|$.  For the volume bound,
apply Fubini along $e_k$: the set on the left has $(e_i,e_j)$-shadow inside
the unit square, and each fiber in the $e_k$ direction is contained in a
chord of $T$ parallel to $e_k$, of length at most $\sqrt2/|Pe_k|$; integrate
over the unit square of area $1$.  Finally
$|Pe_k|^2=1-(w\cdot e_k)^2=(w\cdot e_i)^2+(w\cdot e_j)^2$ as $w$ is a unit
vector.
head: environment

label: lem:calc
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: calculus of the bound functions

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) Positivity of $\mu_*$ is clear for $u>\sqrt2$, and
$\mu_{\mathrm{cap}}<1$ since $u^2-2<u^2$.  For $\mu_*\le\mu_{\mathrm{cap}}$,
square the equivalent inequality
$u(u^2-2)\le(u^2+2)\sqrt{u^2-2}$ and cancel a factor $u^2-2>0$ to get
$u^2(u^2-2)\le(u^2+2)^2$, i.e.\ $0\le6u^2+4$.  The identity $g(\mu_*)=B_1$ follows from
$1-\mu_*^2=8u^2/(u^2+2)^2$, so $\sqrt2/\sqrt{1-\mu_*^2}=(u^2+2)/(2u)$; the
identity $g(\mu_{\mathrm{cap}})=B_2$ from
$1-\mu_{\mathrm{cap}}^2=2/u^2$, so $\sqrt2/\sqrt{1-\mu_{\mathrm{cap}}^2}=u$.

(b) $g'(\mu)=\sqrt2\bigl(-\mu^{-2}+\mu(1-\mu^2)^{-3/2}\bigr)$, whose sign is
that of $\mu^3-(1-\mu^2)^{3/2}$, i.e.\ of $\mu^2-(1-\mu^2)$, i.e.\ negative
for $\mu<1/\sqrt2$ and positive for $\mu>1/\sqrt2$; and
$g(1/\sqrt2)=\sqrt2\cdot\sqrt2+\sqrt2\cdot\sqrt2=4$.

(c) $B_1'(u)=-\dfrac{8\sqrt2\,u}{(u^2-2)^2}+\dfrac12-\dfrac1{u^2}$.  For
$u\in(\sqrt2,2+\sqrt2)$ one has $B_1'<0$: the inequality
$\frac{8\sqrt2u}{(u^2-2)^2}>\frac{u^2-2}{2u^2}$ is equivalent to
$16\sqrt2\,u^3>(u^2-2)^3$, i.e.\ (taking cube roots, both sides positive)
$2\sqrt2\,u>u^2-2$, i.e.\ $u^2-2\sqrt2u-2<0$, which holds exactly for
$u<\sqrt2+2$ (the positive root).  At $u=2+\sqrt2$: $u^2+2=8+4\sqrt2$ and
$u^2-2=4+4\sqrt2$, so
$B_1=\frac{\sqrt2(8+4\sqrt2)}{4+4\sqrt2}+\frac{8+4\sqrt2}{2(2+\sqrt2)}
=\frac{4\sqrt2(2+\sqrt2)}{4(1+\sqrt2)}+\frac{4(2+\sqrt2)}{2(2+\sqrt2)}
=2+2=4$.  For $B_2$:
$B_2'(u)=1-\frac{2\sqrt2}{(u^2-2)^{3/2}}$, which vanishes iff
$(u^2-2)^{3/2}=2\sqrt2$ iff $u^2-2=2$ iff $u=2$, is negative before and
positive after.

(d) On $[2,2+\sqrt2]$, $B_1$ is continuous and strictly decreasing and $B_2$
continuous and strictly increasing, so $B_1-B_2$ is strictly decreasing
there; $B_1(2)=3\sqrt2+\tfrac32>4=B_2(2)$ and
$B_1(2+\sqrt2)=4<B_2(2+\sqrt2)$, so there is a unique root
$u_B\in(2,2+\sqrt2)$.  Direct evaluation gives
$(B_1-B_2)(2.60114)=+7.1\cdot10^{-6}>0$ and
$(B_1-B_2)(2.60115)=-9.6\cdot10^{-6}<0$, whence
$u_B\in(2.60114,2.60115)$.  For the global minimality of $\Psi$ at $u_B$:
if $u\le u_B$ then, since $u_B<2+\sqrt2$ and $B_1$ is decreasing on
$(\sqrt2,2+\sqrt2)$,
$\Psi(u)\ge B_1(u)\ge B_1(u_B)=\Psi(u_B)$; if $u\ge u_B$ then, since
$u_B>2$ and $B_2$ is increasing on $(2,\infty)$,
$\Psi(u)\ge B_2(u)\ge B_2(u_B)=B_1(u_B)=\Psi(u_B)$.  Finally, since $B_1$ is
decreasing and $u_B\ge2.60114$,
$\Psi(u_B)=B_1(u_B)\le B_1(2.60114)=4.28616\ldots<4.2862$.
head: environment

label: thm:B
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:B}
Let $M>\sqrt2$ and let $(B,g)$ traverse $K_M$ weakly.  Then for every
$u\in(\sqrt2,M)$,
\[
\operatorname{vol}(B)\;\le\;\Psi(u),
\]
with $\Psi$ as in \eqref{eq:Psi}.  In particular, for every $M\ge2.61$ the
choice $u=u_B$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:calc}(d) is admissible and
\[
V^{*}(K_M)\;\le\;\Psi(u_B)\;<\;4.2862 ,
\]
covering the corridor of Problem~6.64 ($M=4$) and every larger $M$.
head: environment
name: sharpened upper bound

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $u\in(\sqrt2,M)$, set $c:=1+u<y_t$, and let $\tau_c$, $q$,
$B':=B_{\tau_c}$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:event}.

\emph{Case (i): $B'\cap\{y\le1\}=\emptyset$.}  As in Theorem~\ref{thm:A},
$\operatorname{vol}(B)\le u<B_2(u)\le\Psi(u)$.

\emph{Case (ii): $B'\cap\{y\le1\}\neq\emptyset$.}  Let $T:=T(\tau_c)$ be the
entry tube, $w:=w(\tau_c)$ its axis, $\mu=|w\cdot\hat{y}|$.  By
Lemma~\ref{lem:tiltsharp}, $\mu\in[\mu_*(u),1]$.  Split $B'$ along
$\{y=1\}$ and bound the two parts separately.

\emph{The low part.}  $B'\cap\{y\le1\}$ is contained in
$S_X\cup\mathrm{Stub}(c)\subseteq\{0\le z\le1\}$, in $\{0\le y\}$ by
\eqref{eq:Kfacts}, and in $T$; so its $(y,z)$-shadow lies in $[0,1]^2$ and
Lemma~\ref{lem:chord} (fibers along $\hat{x}$) gives
\[
\operatorname{vol}\bigl(B'\cap\{y\le1\}\bigr)\;\le\;
\frac{\sqrt2}{\sqrt{(w\cdot\hat{y})^2+(w\cdot\hat{z})^2}}\;\le\;\frac{\sqrt2}{\mu}.
\]

\emph{The high part.}  $B'\cap\{y>1\}$ is contained in $\mathrm{Stub}(c)$ (as
$S_X\cap\{y>1\}=\emptyset$), hence its $(x,z)$-shadow lies in $[0,1]^2$ and
each fiber parallel to $\hat{y}$ has length at most $u$ (the stub's height
range $(1,c]$); if $\mu<1$, each such fiber is moreover contained in a chord
of $T$ parallel to $\hat{y}$, of length at most $\sqrt2/\sqrt{1-\mu^2}$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:chord}).  Fubini over the unit square gives
\[
\operatorname{vol}\bigl(B'\cap\{y>1\}\bigr)\;\le\;
\min\Bigl\{u,\ \frac{\sqrt2}{\sqrt{1-\mu^2}}\Bigr\}
\]
(with the convention that the second entry is $+\infty$ when $\mu=1$).

\emph{Combining.}  With $\mu_{\mathrm{cap}}=\mu_{\mathrm{cap}}(u)$ as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:calc}, note that
$\sqrt2/\sqrt{1-\mu^2}\le u\iff\mu\le\mu_{\mathrm{cap}}$.  If
$\mu\in[\mu_*(u),\mu_{\mathrm{cap}}]$, the two caps sum to
$g(\mu)$, and since $g$ is decreasing-then-increasing
(Lemma~\ref{lem:calc}(b)) its maximum over the interval is at an endpoint:
\[
\operatorname{vol}(B)\le g(\mu)\le\max\{g(\mu_*(u)),\,g(\mu_{\mathrm{cap}}(u))\}
=\max\{B_1(u),B_2(u)\}=\Psi(u),
\]
by Lemma~\ref{lem:calc}(a).  If $\mu\in(\mu_{\mathrm{cap}},1]$, the caps sum
to $u+\sqrt2/\mu<u+\sqrt2/\mu_{\mathrm{cap}}=B_2(u)\le\Psi(u)$.  In all
cases $\operatorname{vol}(B)\le\Psi(u)$.

For the numerical form: if $M\ge2.61$ then $u_B<2.60115<2.61\le M$ is
admissible, and Lemma~\ref{lem:calc}(d) gives
$\operatorname{vol}(B)\le\Psi(u_B)<4.2862$.

name: smaller $M$; shape of the bound

label: prop:family
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:family}
Let $u\in(\sqrt2,M)$, $c:=1+u$, and define the two windows
\[
W_1:=[0,1]\times\{1\}\times[0,1],\qquad
W_c:=[0,1]\times\{c\}\times[0,1],
\]
and the family $\mathcal A_u$ of all tubes $T$
(Definition~\ref{def:tubedef}) with axis direction $w$ such that
\[
\text{(i) } |w\cdot\hat{y}|\ge\mu_*(u);\qquad
\text{(ii) } T\cap W_c\neq\emptyset;\qquad
\text{(iii) } T\cap W_1\neq\emptyset .
\]
Then every $(B,g)$ that weakly traverses $K_M$ satisfies
\[
\operatorname{vol}(B)\;\le\;\max\bigl\{u,\ V_{\mathrm{ii}}(u)\bigr\},
\qquad
V_{\mathrm{ii}}(u):=\sup_{T\in\mathcal A_u}
\operatorname{vol}\bigl(T\cap(S_X\cup\mathrm{Stub}(c))\bigr),
\]
and $V_{\mathrm{ii}}(u)\le\Psi(u)<\infty$ with $\Psi$ as in \eqref{eq:Psi}.
head: environment
name: event-forced tube family

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:event} at height $c$ and write $B':=B_{\tau_c}$, so
$\operatorname{vol}(B')=\operatorname{vol}(B)$ and $B'\subseteqS_X\cup\mathrm{Stub}(c)$.  If
$B'\cap\{y\le1\}=\emptyset$ (case (i)), then $\operatorname{vol}(B)\le u$ as in
Theorem~\ref{thm:A}.  Otherwise (case (ii)) consider the tube
$T:=T(\tau_c)$: it contains $B'$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:tube}), hence contains the
touch point $q\in W_c$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:event}) and the deep point
$p^*\in W_1$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:deep}), and its axis satisfies
$|w\cdot\hat{y}|=\mu\ge\mu_*(u)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:tiltsharp}).  So
$T\in\mathcal A_u$ and
$\operatorname{vol}(B)=\operatorname{vol}(B')\le\operatorname{vol}\bigl(T\cap(S_X\cup\mathrm{Stub}(c))\bigr)\le
V_{\mathrm{ii}}(u)$.  Finally, for any $T\in\mathcal A_u$ the two chord
estimates in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:B} apply verbatim to
$T\cap(S_X\cup\mathrm{Stub}(c))$ split along $\{y=1\}$ --- they use only
$\mu\ge\mu_*(u)$ and the shadow geometry of $S_X\cup\mathrm{Stub}(c)$ --- and the
combining step there gives
$\operatorname{vol}(T\cap(S_X\cup\mathrm{Stub}(c)))\le\Psi(u)$.

label: thm:C
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:C}
Let $M>2.2$ and let $(B,g)$ traverse $K_M$ weakly.  Then
\[
\operatorname{vol}(B)\;\le\;3.4083 .
\]
Specifically, a $49{,}513$-leaf branch-and-bound cover of
$\mathcal A_{2.2}$ certifies $V_{\mathrm{ii}}(2.2)\le3.408293$, so
Proposition~\ref{prop:family} with $u=2.2$ gives
$\operatorname{vol}(B)\le\max\{2.2,\,3.408293\}<3.4083$, covering the corridor of
Problem~6.64 ($M=4$) and every $M>2.2$.
head: environment
name: computed upper bound; computer-assisted

label: rem:thmCnature
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:thmCnature}
Theorem~\ref{thm:C} is computer-assisted and its rigor status differs from
Theorems~\ref{thm:A} and~\ref{thm:B}: the computation runs in IEEE double
precision, not in interval arithmetic.  Every comparison, dilation and
per-box bound carries an explicit slack in the conservative direction
($10^{-9}$ relative and $10^{-6}$ absolute per box), the geometry enters
only through outer enclosures, and the certified value sits $\sim0.9$ below
the independent analytic ceiling $\Psi(2.2)=4.96\ldots$, so a floating-point
failure would have to defeat the slacks systematically rather than
marginally.  A re-run under full interval (or rational) arithmetic is the
natural hardening step and is planned as future work; until then
Theorems~\ref{thm:A} and~\ref{thm:B} stand as the fully hand-checkable
ladder beneath Theorem~\ref{thm:C}.

label: rem:gates
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:gates}
The credibility of a computed certificate rests on its test battery.  Four
gates (plus a Monte-Carlo cross-check) were run before any search and re-run
after every change to the evaluator; all pass, and their full output is
archived (Appendix~\ref{app:repro}).
\emph{G1, witness inclusion}: on the certified record traversal of
\cite{OurLB}, at the first crossings of $c=2.5/3.0/3.5$ the record's actual
tube satisfies every constraint of $\mathcal A_u$ with margin (tilt exceeds
the floor by $+0.61/+0.56/+0.48$; both window penetrations are strictly
positive with no tolerance consumed; offsets at radius $\le0.72$ of the
allowed $2.12$), and the evaluator's single-box outer value at that pose
($2.90/2.97/3.70$) dominates both the certified record volume $1.8558404$
and the pose's measured carve mass $1.867$ --- the family provably contains
the one known high-volume traversal, and the evaluator over-counts it, as it
must.
\emph{G2, exactness units}: on two analytically solvable configurations
(axis-aligned; $45^\circ$ in-plane) the computed outer bound dominates the
exact volume and converges to it at the predicted $O(g)$ rate with recorded
constants; the fast correlation matches a direct reference evaluation to
$6.3\cdot10^{-13}$; an independent Monte-Carlo cross-check on $40$ random
tubes found no case with certified value below the Monte-Carlo estimate.
\emph{G3, monotonicity}: box shrinking and grid refinement never increased a
bound ($12$ random boxes, $72$ child comparisons, zero violations).
\emph{G4, restartability}: killing and resuming the search reproduces the
frontier bit-exactly (hash equality).  A failed gate would have stopped the
computation.

name: verification gates

label: rem:mechanism
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:mechanism}
The computed landscape of Table~\ref{tab:landscape} has an interior minimum
in $u$, for the same reason as Theorem~\ref{thm:B}'s optimum at
$u_B\approx2.60$: raising $u$ raises the stub floor, while lowering $u$
weakens the forced-tilt floor $\mu_*(u)$, so nearly horizontal tubes may
rake ever longer stretches of the entry arm.  Pushing below $u=2.2$ indeed
makes the computed bound \emph{worse}: the $u=2.0$ run converged at its
resolution to the larger value $4.0706$.  The computed minimum sits at a
smaller $u$ than $u_B$ because the certified enclosure of
$V_{\mathrm{ii}}(u)$ is sharper than the analytic cap $\Psi(u)$
(at $u=2.2$: $3.41$ versus $4.96$), which shifts the trade-off toward the
lower stub floor.

name: mechanism consistency

label: lem:V2
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:V2}
Let $T,T'$ be tubes with unit-square cross-sections whose axis lines make
angle $\theta\in(0,\pi/2]$.  Then
\[
\operatorname{vol}(T\cap T')\;\le\;\frac{\sqrt2}{\sin\theta}.
\]
head: environment
name: two-tube volume bound

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $e,e'$ be unit axis directions of $T,T'$ with $\angle(e,e')=\theta$, and
let $\bar w:=\frac{e\times e'}{|e\times e'|}$, so $\bar w\perp e,e'$ and
$|\det(e,e',\bar w)|=\sin\theta$.  Use oblique coordinates
$p=\alpha e+\beta e'+\gamma\bar w$, so $dp=\sin\theta\,d\alpha\,d\beta\,
d\gamma$.  Membership $p\in T$ depends only on the projection of $p$ onto
$e^\perp$, namely $\beta e'_\perp+\gamma\bar w+\mathrm{const}$ with
$e'_\perp:=e'-(e\cdot e')e$, $|e'_\perp|=\sin\theta$; at fixed $\gamma$ the
admissible $\beta$ fill an interval of length $\ell(\gamma)/\sin\theta$,
where $\ell(\gamma)\le\sqrt2$ is a chord of the unit square of $T$ along the
fixed direction $e'_\perp/|e'_\perp|$ at offset $\gamma$ (note
$\bar w\in e^\perp$ and $\bar w\perp e'_\perp$).  Symmetrically, membership
$p\in T'$ constrains $\alpha$ to an interval of length
$\ell'(\gamma)/\sin\theta$, where $\gamma\mapsto\ell'(\gamma)$ are parallel
chords of the unit square of $T'$ at perpendicular offset $\gamma$; by
Cavalieri, $\int_\mathbb{R}\ell'(\gamma)\,d\gamma=\operatorname{area}=1$.  Hence
\[
\operatorname{vol}(T\cap T')=\sin\theta\int_\mathbb{R}
\frac{\ell(\gamma)}{\sin\theta}\cdot\frac{\ell'(\gamma)}{\sin\theta}
\,d\gamma
\le\frac{\sup_\gamma\ell(\gamma)}{\sin\theta}\int_\mathbb{R}\ell'(\gamma)\,d\gamma
\le\frac{\sqrt2}{\sin\theta}. \qedhere
\]
head: environment

label: cor:RB
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:RB}
Let $(B,g)$ traverse $K_M$ weakly with $\operatorname{vol}(B)\ge v>\sqrt2$, and let
$a:=R_0^{-1}\hat{x}$, $b:=R_1^{-1}\hat{z}$ be the body-frame axes of the entry
and exit tubes (Lemma~\ref{lem:tube}).  Then the acute angle
$\theta_L$ between the axis \emph{lines} spanned by $a$ and $b$ satisfies
$\sin\theta_L\le\sqrt2/v$, and the net rotation $R_1R_0^{-1}$ has rotation
angle at least $90^\circ-\arcsin(\sqrt2/v)$.  In particular, at the current
certified record volume $v=1.8558404$: every weakly traversing body of at
least this volume satisfies $\theta_L\le49.65^\circ$ and must rotate in total
by more than $40.35^\circ$.
head: environment
name: rotation budget

title: Proof
body_md:
$B$ lies in both body-frame tubes $g_0^{-1}(\mathbb{R}\times[0,1]^2)$ and
$g_1^{-1}([0,1]\times[y_t,y_t+1]\times\mathbb{R})$, with axes $a$ and $b$.  If
$\sin\theta_L>\sqrt2/v$ then Lemma~\ref{lem:V2} gives
$\operatorname{vol}(B)\le\sqrt2/\sin\theta_L<v$, a contradiction; so
$\sin\theta_L\le\sqrt2/v$ (this also covers $\theta_L=0$ trivially).  The
net rotation maps $\hat{x}=R_0a\mapsto R_1a$, and
$\angle(R_1a,\hat{z})=\angle(R_1a,R_1b)=\angle(a,b)=:\theta_v\in[0^\circ,
180^\circ]$, where $\theta_L=\min(\theta_v,180^\circ-\theta_v)$.  By the
spherical triangle inequality the displacement of $\hat{x}$ is
$\angle(\hat{x},R_1a)\ge|\,90^\circ-\theta_v\,|=90^\circ-\theta_L$, and a
rotation moves no unit vector by more than its rotation angle; hence the
rotation angle is at least $90^\circ-\theta_L\ge90^\circ-\arcsin(\sqrt2/v)$.
For $v=1.8558404$: $\arcsin(\sqrt2/v)=49.6438\ldots^\circ\le49.65^\circ$ and
$90^\circ-49.6439^\circ=40.3561\ldots^\circ>40.35^\circ$.
head: environment

label: rem:K1
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:K1}
The two tube containments of Lemma~\ref{lem:tube} \emph{alone} bound
nothing: they leave the relative pose of the two tubes in the body frame
unconstrained, and if the axes coincide the intersection is an infinite tube
of infinite volume.  This degeneracy is realized, not hypothetical: on the
record traversal of \cite{OurLB} the body-frame entry and exit axes agree to
$1.2\cdot10^{-6}$ degrees (the block's long axis remains the traveling axis
through both turns).  Likewise, without the touch clauses of
Lemma~\ref{lem:event}, all containments are satisfied by a body parked deep
in the entry arm, and no volume bound can follow.  Any bound must therefore
couple the tube poses to forced events, as Theorems~\ref{thm:A}
and~\ref{thm:B} do; Corollary~\ref{cor:RB} escapes the degeneracy differently,
by \emph{assuming} a volume and concluding a rotation.
head: environment
name: why the events are indispensable

label: lem:seg
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: no long segments

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\sigma\subseteq B$ be a segment with endpoints $p,q$.  The function
$t\mapsto u(t):=\max\{g_t(p)\cdot\hat{y},\ g_t(q)\cdot\hat{y}\}$ is continuous
(maximum of two continuous functions), $u(0)\le1$ ($B_0\subseteqS_X$) and
$u(1)\ge y_t=1+M>2$ ($B_1\subseteqS_Z$).  As in Lemma~\ref{lem:event} there
is a first time $\tau$ with $u(\tau)=2$.  Write $\sigma_\tau:=g_\tau(\sigma)$,
a segment in $B_\tau\subseteqK$ whose endpoint $y$-values are $\le2$ with
maximum exactly $2$; since $y$ is affine along a segment,
$\sigma_\tau\subseteqK\cap\{y\le2\}=S_X\cup\mathrm{Stub}(2)\subseteq\{0\le z\le1\}$
by \eqref{eq:Kfacts}.  In particular the $z$-extent of $\sigma_\tau$ is at
most $1$.

Project out $z$: $\pi(x,y,z):=(x,y)$.  Then $\pi(\sigma_\tau)$ is a segment
in $\pi(S_X\cup\mathrm{Stub}(2))=\bigl((-\infty,0]\times[0,1]\bigr)\cup
\bigl([0,1]\times[0,2]\bigr)=:\mathrm{Sh}$, with top endpoint
$\tilde q$ at height $y=2$ and $\tilde q_x\in[0,1]$ (a point of height $2>1$
lies in $\mathrm{Stub}(2)$).  Points of $\pi(\sigma_\tau)$ with $y\in(1,2]$ lie in
the strip $[0,1]\times(1,2]$ (the left part of $\mathrm{Sh}$ has $y\le1$).
Let $\tilde p$ be the other endpoint.

If $\tilde p_y>1$, the whole segment lies in $[0,1]\times(1,2]$ and has
length at most $\sqrt{1+1}=\sqrt2$; with the $z$-extent,
$|\sigma|=|\sigma_\tau|\le\sqrt{2+1}<3$.

If $\tilde p_y\le1$, the segment crosses the level $y=1$ at a point $r$,
which is a limit of segment points with $y>1$, hence $r_x\in[0,1]$.  On the
subsegment from $r$ to $\tilde q$: $\Delta y=1$ and $|\Delta x|\le1$, so the
segment's direction satisfies $|dx/dy|\le1$.  On the subsegment from
$\tilde p$ to $r$: $\Delta y=1-\tilde p_y\le1$ (as $y\ge0$ on
$\mathrm{Sh}$), and the direction is the same, so $|\Delta x|\le1$ there
too.  Altogether $|\Delta x|\le2$ and $\Delta y\le2$ over
$\pi(\sigma_\tau)$, so $|\pi(\sigma_\tau)|\le2\sqrt2$, and
$|\sigma|=|\sigma_\tau|\le\sqrt{(2\sqrt2)^2+1^2}=3$.
head: environment

label: cor:convex
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
In a convex body the segment between any two points is contained in the
body, so Lemma~\ref{lem:seg} bounds the diameter by $3$.  By
Lemma~\ref{lem:tube}, $B$ lies in a tube of unit-square cross-section; its
extent along the tube axis is at most its diameter, so
$\operatorname{vol}(B)\le3\cdot1=3$ by Fubini along the axis.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The constant $3$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:seg} is what this argument yields:
optimizing the intermediate height $c$ in its proof leads to
$\bigl(1+\tfrac1{c-1}\bigr)^2+c^2+1$, stationary exactly at $c=2$.  We do
not claim sharpness, although $2\sqrt2$ is the classical planar
segment-passage threshold and full unit $z$-tilt through the corner is
plausible.  Note the contrast: the \emph{diameter} of a general (non-convex)
traversing body is \emph{not} bounded by $3$ --- the record body of
\cite{OurLB} has diameter $\approx3.34$; its far-apart point pairs are
joined only through the bent bulk, in accordance with Lemma~\ref{lem:seg}.
head: environment

label: rem:witness
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:witness}
Every lemma and constant above was checked numerically, in two independent
ways, before being recorded.  (1) \emph{Synthetic}: the chord and slab
estimates and the two-tube bound were tested by exact-chord quadrature and
Monte-Carlo over random tube configurations (observed maxima: $0.67$,
$0.43$, and $0.71$ of the respective proven bounds --- the last consistent
with the conjecture that the sharp two-tube constant is $1/\sin\theta$
rather than $\sqrt2/\sin\theta$, which we do not use); the extremal-point
analysis inside Lemma~\ref{lem:tiltsharp} was verified by direct maximization
over a fine grid of the constraint region, and all quoted roots, enclosures
and evaluations ($u_B$, $\Psi(u_B)$, $f(3.5217)$) were re-derived by
independent optimization.  (2) \emph{Against the record}: on the certified
$512$-pose record traversal of \cite{OurLB}, the forced-tilt inequalities of
Lemmas~\ref{lem:tilt} and~\ref{lem:tiltsharp} hold at every tested event
height with margin (measured tilts $0.68$--$1.00$ against requirements
$0.06$--$0.64$), and the chord inequalities of Lemma~\ref{lem:chord} hold at
\emph{all} $512$ poses of the path with minimum margin $\approx0.7$ in
volume.  A failed check would have refuted the corresponding lemma; none
failed.  The scripts and their JSON outputs are archived with the lower-bound
artifacts.  Theorem~\ref{thm:C}'s computation carries its own, stricter
battery (Remark~\ref{rem:gates} and Appendix~\ref{app:repro}).

label: rem:caveat
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:caveat}
The certified lower bounds of Table~\ref{tab:ladder} are produced by the
evaluation pipeline of \cite{GGTW25}, and one step of that pipeline deserves
a precise caveat: the pipeline's points-to-cubes step (a
$4\times4\times4$-sampled cube counted as inside the corridor) is asserted,
not proven, in the source notebook --- near $K$'s reflex edges a rotated cube
admits $\Theta(h)$-deep excursions between in-corridor sample points.
Point-survival soundness is proved outright in
Appendix~\ref{app:soundness} (axis-convexity of $K$ and $8$-corner exactness
for axis-aligned boxes).  This affects the \emph{absolute} rigor of all
published pipeline numbers equally (the original $1.81$ of \cite{GGTW25}
included), so comparative claims --- the entire ladder of
Table~\ref{tab:ladder} --- are untouched; and nothing in the upper-bound
results of this note rests on the rule.  The step is upgradeable: proving it
(the pipeline's tolerances may absorb the excursions) or quantifying an
$\varepsilon$-correction would upgrade every lower bound's rigor.

label: lem:axisconv
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: axis-convexity

title: Proof
body_md:
Case check on the two frozen coordinates.  Lines parallel to $\hat{x}$: for
$(y,z)\in[0,1]^2$ the intersection is $(-\infty,0]\cup[0,1]=(-\infty,1]$
(the $S_Y$ condition $y\le y_t$ holds automatically as $y_t>1$); for
$y\in(1,y_t]$, $z\in[0,1]$ it is $[0,1]$; for $y\in[y_t,y_t+1]$, $z\ge0$ it
is $[0,1]$; otherwise empty.  Lines parallel to $\hat{y}$: for $x<0$ it is
$[0,1]$ if $z\in[0,1]$, else empty; for $x\in[0,1]$, $z\in[0,1]$ it is
$[0,y_t]\cup[y_t,y_t+1]=[0,y_t+1]$; for $x\in[0,1]$, $z>1$ it is
$[y_t,y_t+1]$.  Lines parallel to $\hat{z}$: for $x<0$, $y\in[0,1]$ it is
$[0,1]$; for $x\in[0,1]$, $y\in[0,y_t)$ it is $[0,1]$; for $x\in[0,1]$,
$y\in[y_t,y_t+1]$ it is $[0,1]\cup[0,\infty)=[0,\infty)$.  All are
intervals.

label: lem:corners
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:corners}
An axis-aligned box with all $8$ corners in $K_M$ is contained in $K_M$.
head: environment
name: $8$-corner exactness

title: Proof
body_md:
Let the box be $[x_0,x_1]\times[y_0,y_1]\times[z_0,z_1]$ with corners in
$K$.  If $x_0<0$: the corners with $x$-coordinate $x_0$ lie in $S_X$ (the
only piece reaching $x<0$), so $y_1\le1$ and $z_1\le1$; and any corner at
$x_1$ lies in $K$ with $y,z\in[0,1]$, forcing $x_1\le1$; then the box lies
in $(-\infty,1]\times[0,1]\times[0,1]\subseteqS_X\cupS_Y$.  If $x_0\ge0$:
all corners lie in $S_Y\cupS_Z$, so $x_1\le1$.  If moreover $z_1\le1$: all
corner $y$-values lie in $[0,y_t+1]$, so every point of the box has
$x\in[0,1]$, $z\in[0,1]$, $y\in[0,y_t+1]$, hence lies in $S_Y$ (if
$y\le y_t$) or in $S_Z$ (if $y\ge y_t$).  If instead $z_1>1$: the four
corners with $z$-coordinate $z_1$ force $y_0,y_1\in[y_t,y_t+1]$, so the box
lies in $[0,1]\times[y_t,y_t+1]\times[0,\infty)=S_Z$.
head: environment
